declarations: System picked from each name's own picture, never the lane tag (R10/R32). All six survivors read as position-system cases (C22, C26): price above structure or at a fresh high on the W/D grid; none is judged by swing rules.

Declared proxies: structure_shift/last swing high for the resistance line, max(fib_swing_low, base_low_20d) for the support line, last_bar colour for the candle-colour flip. cmf (COM proxy) is not served in this packet.
No bracket field is a reason here (R1). C21 weekly read is a house rule, not the author's. No market-wide void exists in my method, so market_void is null.

answers.text: Quote: 'a breakout close, not a set-up.' In my position system the break IS the set-up (C26): buying strength is the entry, not a flaw. Grid agrees: W swing HH/HL, close_vs_swing_high_pct 4.14; D swing HH/HL, dist_to_20bar_high_pct 0.93, last_bar green; H1 above EMA9, 9>21. No coil or retest is required by C26/C27; entry is a buy order 1 tick over bar_high. Fading the break is the swing system's rule, not this case's.

Quote: '20-day RS is the wrong horizon; no pivot breakout.' Horizon point is fair under my C23: 20-day RS is the short ranking, so it is not my position-horizon evidence. But the break already happened: W swing HH/HL, close_vs_swing_high_pct 20.92 above the last weekly swing high. D close_vs_swing_high_pct -4.96 is a pause under the 20-day high, and C27 handles it: trail the buy order to each prior-day high until one breaks. Thesis stands on W structure.
